title: Learned cervical-cancer recurrence models show modest internal discrimination
summary: In a retrospective four-hospital cervical-cancer analysis, learned models estimated recurrence and survival using recorded clinical and pathological factors. The 1,023-person test set was a random split of the same hospital pool. Site-specific recurrence discrimination was modest, and external clinical benefit was not established.
ai_technology: Support vector machine and tree-based survival/classification models
organization: Fudan University; Shanghai Key Laboratory of Female Reproductive Endocrine-Related Diseases; Shanghai Changjiang Science and Technology Development

evidence.tested: The source analyzed 5,112 surgically treated patients, 268 deaths and 343 recurrences, with an 80:20 stratified split, training-only ADASYN and five-fold grid search. For all 22 variables, test recurrence AUC was .794 for SVM versus .785 for logistic regression; site-specific recurrence AUC was .781 versus .776. SVM local/distant test sensitivities were .472/.424 at the represented operating points.
evidence.unknown: The source calls the test external, but Methods randomly divide patients pooled from the same four hospitals; this is internal evaluation. Some feature subsets are selected from whole-cohort Cox associations, and containment is not established. Inputs include postoperative pathology/adjuvant treatment, so this is not preoperative prediction or a causal treatment-effect model. Recurrence event counts differ 343 versus 344 across source locations. Binary risk endpoints do not supply a frozen future prediction horizon. Source claims of a universally best model are not supported across all displayed table cells; no clinical surveillance benefit is measured.
evidence.ai_role: Learned classifiers and representations evaluate a defined clinical staging or recurrence target; conventional clinicopathologic associations are not separately counted as AI discoveries.

source_review.scope: Original patient cohort, computational Methods and represented Results actually read
